# Python Basics

Python is a dynamically typed, interpreted programming language known
for its readable syntax. Variables are created by assignment, functions
are defined with the def keyword, and indentation is used to delimit
code blocks instead of braces. Lists, dictionaries, and sets are built
in container types that make it easy to store and manipulate collections
of data without importing extra libraries.

# Debugging Tips

When a program misbehaves, start by reproducing the bug reliably and
adding print statements or breakpoints near the suspected code path.
Read the traceback carefully, since it usually points to the exact line
and exception type that caused the failure. Version control tools like
git bisect can help you find the exact commit that introduced a
regression when the bug has been present for a while.
